[Ruha+ti]  CL=8 [Ruhanaṃ rūḷhī. Rū. 621.] Growing or ascending is rūḷhī.
[Dabbaṃ ruhati anugacchatīti rūḷhī,] Rūḷhī is that which grows on or follows a substance.
[dabbassa vā upari ruhitabbā āropetabbāti rūḷhī.] Or rūḷhī is that which should be grown or raised upon a substance.
[Nimitte sati vā asati vā asati vā dabbe ruhati gacchati pavattati vā rūḷhī.] Whether there is a cause or not, or whether there is a substance or not, rūḷhī is that which grows, goes, or proceeds.
[Saddākyī put sit kyay, 575. Nīti, sutta. 525. Rūḍhi-saṃ, pyā addhamāga.] References to various grammatical texts.
When compared with Sanskrit and two other languages, in Pali too, only the word rū with long vowel and rūḷhī seem to be the old reading. In place of ti-paccaya in Rū. 621, the correct reading should be [ruhanaṃ rūḷhi].
In Nirutti-page-505, it is said [tipaccayamhi-ruhanaṃ rūḷhi, niruhanaṃ nirūḷhi, viruhanaṃ virūḷhi], therefore according to this teacher"s opinion, rūḷhi should have the correct reading with rassa i (short "i").
(1) Established or grown in usage.

(3) Evident or clear.
